items.title: Privacy egress monitor
items.summary: Live tracking of what certified/legitimate apps actually send — moving CounterSpy from 'is this spyware?' to 'this app is trusted, but here's what it's exfiltrating; do you consent?'. A per-process egress observer (destination/volume tracking, consent deltas). v1 (now in development): a live TUI 'egress top' via sudo-CLI observation (nettop + lsof), observe-only. Rationale: the v0.3.0 feedback loop measures false positives among flagged apps; the next risk surface is the apps NOT flagged — notarized/allowlisted software that over-collects. Rhymes with the egress-only invariant: watch egress because egress is where the risk lives.

items.title: Egress destination enrichment via packet capture
items.summary: Enrich the egress monitor's destinations with real names and per-flow volume via a root packet tap (pktap/tcpdump) with process attribution — surfacing TLS SNI / DNS names instead of bare cloud IPs. Deferred from v0.4.0 for scope and sequencing: the v0.4.0 observe loop (nettop + lsof) establishes the per-app egress picture first; packet capture adds pcap parsing and a heavier data path best layered on a working monitor. Still root-CLI-feasible (no entitlement), unlike the Network Extension path.

items.title: Egress payload / content inspection
items.summary: See the actual CONTENT of what an app exfiltrates, not just destinations/volume and capability-inferred candidates. Requires TLS interception — installing a MITM trust anchor and decrypting flows — which is invasive, itself spyware-shaped, and a trust-sensitive move for an anti-spyware tool. Deferred deliberately and gated behind explicit, per-run user consent and a very high bar. Until then, v0.4.0 answers 'what is being exfiltrated' by INFERENCE (TCC capability x egress), never by reading payloads. Recorded so the ambition is tracked, not silently promised.
